name: Penthesilea
epigraph: Outside Penthesilea does an outside exist? Or, no matter how far you go from the city, will you only pass from one limbo to another, never managing to leave it?

canonical_stones.label: Low buildings with backs turned
canonical_stones.detail: Shallow plaster structures facing away from the chalk road, exposing blank rear walls and drainpipes.

canonical_stones.label: Plank fences
canonical_stones.detail: Weather-bleached uneven timber palings bordering dusty lots that neither enclose nor exclude.

canonical_stones.label: Corrugated-iron sheds
canonical_stones.detail: Ribbed zinc lean-tos and storage sheds rattling faintly in the flat plain wind.

canonical_stones.label: Patches of cabbages
canonical_stones.detail: Dusty pale-jade cabbage rows planted in chalky soil directly between warehouses and fences.

canonical_stones.label: Cemeteries
canonical_stones.detail: Scattered burial plots of tilted limestone markers and dry weeds recurring hours apart.

canonical_stones.label: Snaggle-toothed walls
canonical_stones.detail: Shallow facades, very tall beside very low like a snaggle-toothed comb, falsely promising a thickening center.

canonical_stones.label: Rusty carnival wheel
canonical_stones.detail: Skeletal oxidized Ferris wheel and low-hanging fairground frame stranded in an empty gravel lot.

canonical_stones.label: Stray tollbooths
canonical_stones.detail: Isolated booths with peeling striped arms standing across tracks where no city wall or gate exists.

canonical_stones.label: Workshops
canonical_stones.detail: Vulcanizers, scrap-metal sheds, oil drums, and intermittent weld sparks along unnamed crossroads.

canonical_stones.label: Shambles
canonical_stones.detail: Bleached concrete market shambles with iron hooks and shallow runnels at the edge of vacant lots.
